summary.text: Daniel Simonds is the Democratic candidate for the Maine House of Representatives, District 73, in the November 3, 2026 general election, where he faces incumbent Republican Michael Soboleski.
A forester and consultant who lives in Rangeley, he described himself in a Ballotpedia survey as a beginner at politics.

paragraphs.text: Simonds said in a Ballotpedia survey that he studied forestry at the University of Maine and built a career in the forest products industry, including 20 years managing woodlands.

He said he came to Rangeley with his wife, Lucy, in 1990, was laid off when a large paper company left the town, and then founded a consulting business specializing in environmental standards for the wood products industry.
Simonds won the Democratic primary on June 9, 2026, with 1,031 votes.

In the survey, he said government should work for the common good, that concentrated wealth and political power are a defining challenge, and that rural District 73 communities deserve to be heard on their own terms.
